significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a "read-time magnitude of the internal update predicts which downstream ripple queries the model will answer correctly" and varies selectively by entailment type, a form-(iii) predictive coupling rather than merely an existence claim. It would establish both a phenomenon—entailed propositions change internally before being queried—and a limited mechanism concerning computation timing and representational propagation, fixing expectations about later query success and whether failures originate during ingestion rather than retrieval. RippleEdits (Cohen et al., 2023) operationalizes ripple effects as behavioral satisfaction of logical constraints, so a verified negative here would also matter by ruling out spontaneous read-time propagation and supporting on-demand, query-time computation; the negative is stronger than simply failing to locate a direction. True and false are distinguishable, and the topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic research on LLM beliefs would not itself imply the claim's specific temporal ordering, entailment-type selectivity, or predictive coupling.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "read-time internal-ripple diagnostic," whose magnitude is proposed as a predictor of downstream ripple-query success. It is ex ante because the claim says failures are "visible internally at ingestion time" and could be predicted "before spending multi-hop QA," leaving an action window for context-management, knowledge-editing, or agent-memory pipelines. After per-model probe re-extraction, the substantive prediction still travels as a qualitative relation—larger selective read-time updates forecast greater downstream success across symmetric, inverse, transitive, and inheritance entailments—although it does not specify transferable numerical thresholds. The hypothesis is framed for LLMs and multiple entailment classes, with downstream uptake by researchers and practitioners who audit or gate updates; the topic-substitution check fails because belief research alone supplies neither this diagnostic nor its pre-query lead time.
